ML three-step latent transition analysis (covariates and distal outcomes)

lta3step.Rd

Re-estimates the structural part of a fitted LTA with covariates and/or distal outcomes by the bias-adjusted maximum-likelihood three-step method (Vermunt 2010; Asparouhov & Muthén 2014, Mplus Web Note 15), so that the measurement model is not changed by the auxiliary variables.

Usage

lta3step(
  object,
  data,
  covariates = NULL,
  covariates_on = "all",
  interaction = FALSE,
  distal = NULL,
  distal_categorical = NULL,
  distal_wave = NULL,
  distal_variances = "equal",
  starts = c(20, 4),
  seed = 20261119,
  maxiter = 5000,
  tol = 1e-10
)

Arguments

object

A fitted LTA (lta()).

data

The data frame object was fitted to (same rows), holding the covariates and distal outcomes.

covariates

Covariates of the latent classes (one-step; numeric columns, dummy-code factors): a selection such as c(female, ses) for time-invariant covariates used at every wave, or list(x_1, x_2, x_3) with one selection per wave for time-varying covariates (wave t's columns enter the initial class at wave 1 and the transition into wave t). Mplus c1 ON x; c2 ON c1 x; .... Rows with a missing covariate are deleted (as in Mplus).

covariates_on

"all" (initial classes and transitions, default), "initial" (c1 ON x only) or "transitions".

interaction

TRUE: covariate effects on the transitions differ by the class at the previous wave (Mplus c2 ON x inside MODEL c1:, User's Guide Ex. 8.14).

distal

Distal outcomes of the class at distal_wave (default: last wave), estimated jointly with the LTA (one step): numeric columns, normal within class (class-specific means).

distal_categorical

The columns of distal that are categorical (class-specific probabilities).

distal_wave

Wave whose class the distal outcomes depend on (default: last).

distal_variances

"equal" (default) or "varying" within-class variances of continuous distal outcomes.

starts

Length-2 integer vector: number of stage-1 random starts and of stage-2 starts iterated to convergence (Mplus STARTS). A single number is recycled. The default c(100, 20) with 20 stage-1 EM iterations corresponds to Mplus STARTS = 100 20; STITERATIONS = 20 (the Mplus defaults are 20 4 and 10 iterations).

seed

Random seed for the random starts.

maxiter

Maximum number of EM iterations in stage 2.

tol

Convergence tolerance: change in the log-likelihood per case.

Value

A latentmix LTA; use coeftable(), parameters() and transitions() (at).

Details

Step 1 is the fitted LTA object; step 2 assigns every case to its most likely class at each wave (a wave without observed indicators is missing); step 3 fits an LTA in which the most likely class of each wave is a single nominal indicator whose response probabilities are fixed at that wave's classification errors (classification_table(object, wave = t)$errors), with the covariates on the initial classes and the transitions and/or distal outcomes of the class at distal_wave. This is the manual three-step LTA of Mplus (NOMINAL modal classes with fixed logits); the results agree with Mplus on the validation case. Standard errors treat the classification errors as known.

References

Vermunt, J. K. (2010). Latent class modeling with covariates: Two improved three-step approaches. Political Analysis, 18(4), 450–469. doi:10.1093/pan/mpq025

Asparouhov, T., & Muthén, B. (2014). Auxiliary variables in mixture modeling: Three-step approaches using Mplus. Structural Equation Modeling, 21(3), 329–341. doi:10.1080/10705511.2014.915181

See also

lta() (one-step covariates), r3step() and bch() (wave).

Examples

data(substance)
# \donttest{
# does parental monitoring predict grade-8 status and the transitions? (three steps)
t3 <- lta(substance, waves = list(alc_1:mj_1, alc_2:mj_2, alc_3:mj_3), K = 3)
#> Starting Julia ...
s3 <- lta3step(t3, substance, covariates = c(female, monitor))
ct <- coeftable(s3, ref = 1)
ct[ct$term == "monitor", c("parameter", "estimate", "se", "p")]
#>          parameter      estimate           se p
#> 3  C1#2 ON MONITOR -0.5144631114 2.072849e+41 1
#> 6  C1#3 ON MONITOR -0.7634801139 8.411290e+40 1
#> 14 C2#2 ON MONITOR  0.0302414275 1.452308e+42 1
#> 16 C2#3 ON MONITOR  0.0002324823 1.833056e+42 1
#> 24 C3#2 ON MONITOR -0.1963428881 1.787499e+28 1
#> 26 C3#3 ON MONITOR -0.0836929599 7.850681e+27 1
# }
